ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Serial-transfer ALE campaign is an evolution/selection engineering action (Q1), implemented by the current authors (Q2), and represents a chosen strain-development strategy rather than a measurement (Q3).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli W in M9 + 0.2% (v/v) glycerol via serial batch transfer every 12 h at 37 °C with stepwise lowering of initial OD600 (0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016) for ~1300 generations, followed by single-clone isolation (CY02).
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Action described in 4_2_ale_and_strain_isolation_p001-p003 and Abstract; no M0-M11 action code assigned because the runtime contract provides no mapping table in this call.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Pre-existing knowledge gap stated before the action: glycerol is a non-preferential, low-energy-density carbon source for productive fermentation, and wild-type E. coli metabolic networks are not optimized for glycerol utilization (Abstract; 3_discussion_p001 citing prior glycerol ALE studies).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement for the outcome (growth and uptake rates measured pre/post) combined with literature_precedent for choosing the ALE approach; legacy hard/soft slot filled as 'hard' because the decision's effect was directly measured in this paper.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: ALE was chosen as a robust top-down approach previously demonstrated to improve glycerol fitness in E. coli (Cheng et al. 2014; Herring et al. 2006; Ibarra et al. 2002; Kang et al. 2019, cited in 3_discussion_p001).

generalizable_rule.statement: Serial-batch ALE under glycerol limitation can improve glycerol-utilization fitness (specific growth rate and glycerol uptake) of E. coli W.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli W; M9 minimal + 0.2% (v/v) glycerol; 37 °C; 50 mL/250 mL flasks; 12 h transfer cycle; ~1300 generations; single endpoint clone CY02.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other hosts, carbon sources, products, and culture formats untested; number of independent parallel ALE lineages not reported; transferability of specific mutations (glpK T235M, crp R209H) to other backgrounds not established.
generalizable_rule.evidence_basis: literature_analogy (reason_nature) + experimental_measurement in this paper (EXP1, EXP3)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Chromosomal insertion of the mtGAD expression cassette is an explicit construct design action (Q1) used in this study's strains (Q2; attribution caveat below) and is a design choice for GABA biosynthesis (Q3). Caveat: the mtGAD enzyme variant itself originates from prior studies by the same group (Choi et al. 2015; Thu Ho et al. 2013; Hou and Kang 2018), so the enzyme-design portion is attributed to background citations; only its deployment in these strains is current-study.
ddr_annotations.design_action: Use of a mutant glutamate decarboxylase B (mtGAD) under the PLtetQ-1 promoter, inserted into the chromosome (lacZ locus per 'lacZ:mtGAD' strain label), yielding constitutive expression because E. coli W lacks the cognate repressor and avoiding antibiotic markers during culture.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Described in 2_6_gaba_production_in_e_coli_w_p001; insertion site inferred only from the strain label 'lacZ:mtGAD' in 2_7_p002 and marked as such.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: GABA is produced from L-glutamate by GAD, but wild-type GAD is inadequately active at physiological pH; the mtGAD variant remains catalytically active at physiological pH (prior-work knowledge cited at 2_6_p001, preceding its use here).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent for enzyme choice; experimental_measurement for in-study performance (GABA titers measured in EXP9-EXP12).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: mtGAD selected because prior studies showed it is catalytically active at physiological pH and suitable for fermentative GABA production (Choi et al. 2015; Hou and Kang 2018; Thu Ho et al. 2013).

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Switching the production medium from M9 minimal to amino-acid-rich LB and screening glycerol concentration is a fermentation-condition design action (Q1), performed by the current authors (Q2), and a deliberate design choice to relieve growth inefficiency (Q3).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Replace M9 minimal medium (0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract) with LB supplemented with 2% (v/v) glycerol for GABA production; glycerol concentration selected by growth-rate proxy screening (highest growth at 2%; data in Fig. S7, supplement unavailable).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Measured prior result: final GABA concentration in M9 minimal medium showed negligible difference between wild-type and CY02 (0.06 ± 0.01 g/L each, 2_6_p002), together with pre-action reasoning about growth inefficiency under carbon limitation, high L-glutamate biosynthetic cost from glycerol, and limiting glycerol supply (2_6_p003).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (GABA titers before/after the switch) plus screening_result for the glycerol-concentration proxy screen; the screen's underlying data (Fig. S7) are in the unavailable supplement, lowering auditable support for the 2% optimum.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Rationale given before/with the decision: growth inefficiency under carbon-limited excess substrate can be restored by amino acid supplementation (Prensky 2021; Russell and Cook 1995; Waschina 2016), and GABA production was assumed growth-coupled; combines mechanistic reasoning with cited literature.

generalizable_rule.statement: For growth-coupled GABA production from glycerol in E. coli W backgrounds, amino-acid-rich LB medium with 2% (v/v) glycerol yields higher stationary-phase GABA titers than M9 minimal medium with 0.2% (v/v) glycerol.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: E. coli W wild-type, glpK^m, crp^m, glpK^m crp^m and CY02 carrying mtGAD; LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol; 50 mL/250 mL shake flasks; 37 °C, 200 rpm.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other media, glycerol concentrations (screen data unavailable), scales, products, and hosts untested; growth-rate proxy may not hold for non-growth-coupled products.

alternatives_considered.alternative: M9 minimal medium + 0.2% glycerol + 50 mg/L yeast extract
alternatives_considered.fate: tested and superseded for GABA production
alternatives_considered.reason: negligible GABA titer difference between wild-type and CY02 (0.06 ± 0.01 g/L each)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Targeted deletion of ackA, mgsA and gabT is a deliberate gene-knockout engineering action (Q1), constructed by the current authors in CY02 and wild-type backgrounds (Q2), and constitutes a rational flux-redirection design choice (Q3).
ddr_annotations.design_action: lambda-Red-mediated deletion of ackA (acetate kinase), mgsA (methylglyoxal synthase) and gabT (4-aminobutyrate aminotransferase), singly and in combination, in CY02 (yielding CY02_ΔackA, CY02_ΔgabT, CY02_ΔmgsA, double knockouts and CY02_TKO) and in the wild-type lacZ:mtGAD background.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Target selection and construction stated in 2_7_metabolic_engineering_of_e_coli_w_to_improve_gaba_production_p001; double-knockout construction is implied by Results/Fig. S8 but not explicitly described (see conflicts).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Measured prior results and cited mechanisms preceding the action: (i) pronounced acetate overflow measured in CY02 (EXP8); (ii) reported risk of cytotoxic methylglyoxal accumulation from glpK-mutant-driven glycerol influx (Freedberg et al. 1971); (iii) known GABA re-consumption via the gabT GABA-shunt (prior GABA engineering literature cited in 2_7_p001).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (acetate overflow and post-knockout GABA titers measured in this paper) combined with literature_precedent for target selection.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Each target was justified by a pathway-level mechanism stated before the results: re-route acetate-overflow carbon (ackA), curb methylglyoxal toxicity and lactate side-pathway (mgsA), and block GABA degradation (gabT); supported by cited prior GABA/glycerol engineering studies.

generalizable_rule.statement: In the glycerol-evolved E. coli W CY02 background, combined deletion of ackA, mgsA and gabT increases GABA titer and specific productivity (1.5- and 1.6-fold over CY02; 0.59 ± 0.04 g/L and 0.13 ± 0.02 g/L/hr).
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: CY02 and wild-type lacZ:mtGAD backgrounds; LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol; shake flasks at 37 °C; single, double and triple knockouts compared.
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Benefit NOT reproduced in the wild-type background (background-dependent epistasis); not tested in other hosts, media, carbon sources, or at process scale; single knockouts decreased GABA relative to CY02.
